title: Rewrite SSO serialization layer and constrain crypto ABI surface
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Refactor the SSO serialization/deserialization layer to remove unsafe transitive crypto ABI exposure, upgrade JOSE/JWT and OAuth libraries to their latest LTS versions, and harden the token validation hot path for both performance and security. This reduces attack surface from FFI/ABI leaks and prepares the runtime for an upcoming FIPS-compatible build.
acceptance_criteria: Replace ad-hoc binary serialization in saml/assertion path with explicit, versioned wire format and backward-compatible parsers
Upgrade github.com/square/go-jose and golang-jwt packages to vetted LTS versions and eliminate deprecated dependency forks
Introduce a thin crypto-abstraction boundary with explicit whitelist of symbols; no direct transitive FFI calls from high-level auth code
End-to-end tests passing for SSO flows (SAML/OIDC) including signature validation and replay protection
Performance: token validation 95th percentile latency reduced by at least 20% in local benchmark suite
Staged rollout with feature flag and automatic rollback on error spike or correctness regression
notes_and_plan: Background: Over time the SSO code accumulated multiple binary serializers and direct FFI calls into native crypto helpers. These increase risk (ABI/FFI symbol surface) and make audits harder. This ticket consolidates and trims the surface while upgrading critical crypto libraries.
Phase 1 (spike): prototype pure-Go parser for assertion payloads and measure allocations (completed 2025-02-17)
Phase 2 (implementation): implement versioned wire format, add compatibility shim for older tokens, and introduce crypto abstraction (in progress)
Phase 3 (upgrade): bump JOSE/JWT/OAuth libs and remove deprecated forks; run dependency SCA and fuzzing harnesses
Phase 4 (rollout): feature-flagged canary across 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic error budget gating
Monitoring: Add specific SLO dashboards for token-validation latency and sign/verify error rates; synthetic SSO smoke tests every 5 minutes
Risk: edge-cases with legacy enterprise customers still sending deprecated assertion formats. We will provide a compatibility shim for 90 days and notify customer success teams.
implementation_notes: Introduce auth/serial v2 package with explicit TestVectors and serde tests
Wrap native crypto calls behind auth/crypto/provider.go interface and allow injection in tests
Drop two small Cgo helpers previously used for ASN.1 quirks; emulate behavior in Go to reduce FFI burden
Add unit tests for tampering detection, canonicalization, and whitespace normalization in assertions
Benchmark harness: token-validator-bench.go added to infra/bench with reproducible Docker image
Update SDKs: surface any API contract changes in server logs and document migration notes for SDK teams
qa_plan: Unit tests and property tests for new serializer/parser
Integration tests for SAML and OIDC with locally-run IdP mock
Fuzzing job for 48 hours against parser inputs in CI
Security scan (SCA) and dependency CVE check before merging
Canary smoke checks and token replay tests post-deploy
